question.text: Let in <math><mo>∆</mo><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi></math> the coordinates of <math><mi>A</mi></math> are <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi></mi><mn>0</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math> Internal angle bisector of <math><mi>∠</mi><mi>A</mi><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi></math> is <math><mi>x</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>y</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></math> and mid-point of <math><mi>B</mi><mi>C</mi></math> is <math><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi></mi><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfenced><mo>.</mo></math> Then, the ordinate of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>C</mi></math> is

solution.text:
Reflection of A0,0 about the line x-y+1=0 is -1,1 which lies on BC

The equation of BC is x=-1 (line passing through -1,1 & -1,3)
⇒B is the point of intersection of x=-1 and x-y+1=0

The point B is -1,0
Hence, the coordinates of C are-1,6 (since, the mid point of  B & C is -1,3)
